blocks.text: Jeremiah 2 is near the beginning of a received book that combines poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, nation oracles, and an appendix. This is the product of a long compositional and textual history. That does not require a reader to solve how every part was formed; it is a reminder to read chapter 2 as prophetic poetry within a book whose literary forms and arrangement are varied.

A practical outline of the Masoretic form of Jeremiah places chapters 2–25 together after the opening chapter. The outline is a reading aid, not a decision about the book's composition. It can help a reader keep chapter 2 within the first broad movement of prophetic material without flattening its poetry into a simple chronological report.
